correctness.rationale: The seven transient-state backward equations uniquely determine exact mean extinction times. Symbolic inversion gives the stated rational T_center and T_full expressions in s=a+b and p=ab. The factorized center comparisons prove exact concentrated/balanced/tie regimes including boundaries, and an explicitly positive polynomial proves full-occupancy balancing. A standalone checker passed six symbolic identities, 240 independent rational CTMC solves, and 21 exact regime comparisons. Rescaling e is exact. No extrapolation from testing is used as proof.

evidence: Ross and Pollett (2009), https://www.maths.uq.edu.au/MASCOS/MODSIM09/RossPollett.pdf, use a homogeneous colonization coefficient c and choose between increasing c and decreasing the extinction parameter e; their Discussion explicitly identifies patch-targeted/weighted allocation as future work.

Artzy-Randrup and Stone (2010), doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1000876, derive a deterministic linear age-structured spectral-radius criterion; this does not imply equality or inequality of expected finite CTMC extinction times.
Etienne and Heesterbeek (2001), doi:10.1086/321986, discuss colonization versus local extinction investments in the abstract but do not therein state the exact three-patch product law.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The primary fully inspected two papers have substantially different mathematical objectives or feasible-control sets. The generality of the stochastic management literature remains a residual risk; no claim is made that abstract-only papers were entirely checked.

evidence: Artzy-Randrup and Stone show deterministic persistence is controlled by the leading eigenvalue, which here equals sqrt(a²+b²) and always favors concentration; it does not compare T_center and T_full.

The Ross–Pollett 2009 full article explicitly states that the simple model has colonization rate c shared across patches and that targeting or weighted allocation is an unexamined modification (Discussion, pp. 6–7).
The new result gives T_center(s,p) and T_full(s,p) and proves opposite allocation policies for the same budget when 0<s<1.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The deterministic spectral claim is strictly weaker for this stochastic objective; homogeneous-budget rules do not imply a two-link constrained split or its seed-dependent threshold. Earlier three-site directional-imbalance results constrain *outbound vs inbound* rates and optimize distinct persistence observables, so they neither imply the new left/right symmetric-edge phase diagram nor its central-seed threshold. Potential unpublished exact reductions remain a historical-priority caveat.

originality.rationale: Full accessible foundational texts were examined by model, observable and control set, not title alone. The nearest strong inspected management work studies homogeneous colonization versus extinction improvements and explicitly identifies weighted targeting as an unexamined modification. The nearest spectral source gives a deterministic proxy but no stochastic finite-absorption optimizer. Full journal texts of two plausible predecessors remain inaccessible, so the priority finding is provisional and not an assertion of exhaustive novelty.
residual_risks: Full journal text of Etienne–Heesterbeek (2001) was not available for a decisive statement-by-statement comparison.
Full Ross–Pollett (2010) journal text was not available, although the earlier full conference exposition was inspected.
Detailed small-network CTMC identities may have appeared in uncatalogued dissertations or epidemiological literature under distinct terminology.
The full Mountford et al. (2016) article was not inspected; available exposition is asymptotic, but no entire-document exclusion is asserted.

value.rationale: The control set and observables are natural ecological design questions: splitting a fixed corridor investment among two links, with contrasting initial occupancy scenarios. The theorem gives an exact, equality-inclusive budget threshold, a complete allocation classification on the minimal nontrivial path, and a non-implied mismatch against a standard spectral persistence proxy. It identifies when protecting rare colonization founders and maintaining an established community require different spatial design. No general ecological field efficacy is asserted.
